correctness.rationale: The September source gives m(H_a)>=tau(a)/c1 and m(B_g(a))<=c3 S_g(a). Dividing gives the exact conditional upper bound c1 c3 S_g(a)/tau(a). The August companion proves tau(a)/f(a)->infinity for every computable decreasing f->0. Setting f=1/h yields 1/tau(a)=o(h(a)), hence the master result for every computable increasing divergent h. The four special cases use the source's own series estimates; no unproved estimate of the universal tail is introduced.

value.rationale: The paper's motivating question is naturally conditional on high complexity, but its theorems report absolute universal mass. The accepted theorem rigorously converts those estimates into true conditional prevalence and shows that all four qualitative decay regimes survive normalization. The fact that the normalization loss is smaller than every prescribed computable divergent factor is a distinctive consequence of the universal tail's noncomputably slow decay and is reusable for future bad-set estimates in the same structureless framework.
